checks.reason: No defect found. I copied the pre-change RegExpRouter into a scratch file and ran it against the patched one on 20,000 random route sequences (ALL/GET/POST; static, param, regexp-param, optional and wildcard segments). The new router throws in add() exactly when the old one threw at match(), and it never throws during match(). Where both succeed, the matched handlers and params are identical. The existing reg-exp-router and smart-router tests pass. The new tests also pass, including the ones for `/:x{.}`, ALL versus a specific method in both orders, and capturing `id` after `/w/*/x`.
